#02 Click xpath=//div[contains(@class,'spotlight-item-title')][normalize-space()='Eclipse Series']/ancestor::div[contains(@class,'spotlight-item')] Click Eclipse Series spotlight image/link
⚠ ErrorElement is not interactable — CSS visibility:hidden. This is a real source code issue.
🔍 Element Inspector · <div> click click to zoom
🔍 Root Cause
[A] WEBSITE BUG — The .spotlight-item element (or one of its ancestors) has visibility: hidden applied via CSS, making it non-interactable even though display: block and pointer-events: auto are set. The element exists in the DOM and is visually rendered (opacity: 1, display: block), but visibility: hidden suppresses interaction. This is likely a CSS animation/AOS (Animate On Scroll) initialization state that never resolved to visibility: visible, or a deliberate CSS rule that was incorrectly applied to the container rather than just a child overlay element.
❌ Problematic Code
/* Likely in the theme's CSS — the spotlight-item or its wrapper
   is being set to visibility:hidden, possibly as an AOS initial state
   or a hover/reveal pattern that never transitions back to visible */

.spotlight-item {
  visibility: hidden; /* or inherited from a parent rule */
}

/* OR an AOS-related rule such as: */
[data-aos] {
  visibility: hidden;
}
/* that is not being overridden once the animation completes on the parent container */
✅ Fixed Code
/* Ensure the spotlight-item container is visible once AOS has initialized.
   In the theme's CSS (e.g. base.css or the section's stylesheet), add or verify: */

.spotlight-item {
  visibility: visible;
}

/* If the visibility:hidden is coming from an AOS parent rule leaking onto
   the .spotlight-item wrapper, scope it more tightly so only the
   image-element child receives the AOS hidden state: */

.spotlight-item [data-aos]:not(.aos-animate) {
  visibility: hidden;
}

.spotlight-item [data-aos].aos-animate {
  visibility: visible;
}

/* Do NOT apply visibility:hidden to .spotlight-item itself —
   only to the inner animated child elements. */
📋 What To Do
  • **Inspect the theme CSS** for any rule that sets visibility: hidden on .spotlight-item, .spotlight-image-wrapper, or a parent section container — correct or remove it.
  • **Check AOS configuration**: the <image-element> inside uses data-aos="image-fade-in" and already has aos-animate applied, meaning AOS fired correctly for the child — but if a parent rule sets visibility: hidden on .spotlight-item as an AOS initial state, it may never have been reset to visible.
  • **Verify the fix** by inspecting computed visibility on .spotlight-item at runtime after page load; it must resolve to visible.
  • **The test selector itself is correct** — the XPath finds the right element — so no changes to the YAML are needed once the CSS is fixed.
  • If a quick fix is needed immediately, add .spotlight-item { visibility: visible !important; } to the theme's custom CSS override file as a temporary patch while the root AOS/CSS rule is properly investigated.

Verify the front end styling in 375 px
Manual front-end style audit against the Figma "Departure Design" file at the 375px breakpoint. No specific test case document existed for this - findings are consolidated here per-property. CAVEAT: this Figma file defines only a 1440px desktop layout - there is no mobile/375px frame or per-breakpoint type scale value anywhere in the file, so full mobile compliance cannot be verified against a mockup that does not exist; the checks below are best-effort, assuming the type scale's blank "Mobile" column means "inherit the desktop value" absent a distinct spec.
Failed ▼
# Action Expected / Result Status
#01 Verify xpath=//div[@id='NavDrawer']//a[contains(@class,'mobile-nav__link') and normalize-space()='Explore'] style font-family contains "Noto Sans" Same Noto Sans expectation as desktop (H5 - Navi Bar) - the mobile drawer's nav links currently inherit the same Noto Serif styling as the desktop nav bar
⚠ ErrorStyle "font-family" expected to contain "Noto Sans" but got ""Noto Serif", serif"
🔍 Element Inspector · <a> verify_style_contains click to zoom
🔍 Root Cause
[A] WEBSITE BUG — The mobile-nav__link element for "Explore" in the #NavDrawer is rendering with font-family: "Noto Serif", serif instead of the expected "Noto Sans" sans-serif font. According to the Figma spec, the mobile navigation links should use the sans-serif Noto Sans typeface, but the current theme CSS is applying a serif font family to this element. This is a genuine styling defect in the theme code — the wrong font-family rule is being applied to .mobile-nav__link or one of its ancestors in the mobile drawer context.
❌ Problematic Code
/* Current theme CSS — likely in theme.css or a section stylesheet */
.mobile-nav__link,
.mobile-nav__link--top-level {
  font-family: "Noto Serif", serif;
}
✅ Fixed Code
/* Corrected theme CSS */
.mobile-nav__link,
.mobile-nav__link--top-level {
  font-family: "Noto Sans", sans-serif;
}
📋 What To Do
  • Open the theme's CSS file (e.g., assets/theme.css or assets/timber.css) and locate the rule setting font-family on .mobile-nav__link or .mobile-nav__link--top-level.
  • Change the value from "Noto Serif", serif to "Noto Sans", sans-serif to align with the Figma spec for mobile navigation typography.
  • Also check parent selectors (e.g., #NavDrawer, .mobile-nav, .drawer) for any inherited font-family: "Noto Serif" rule that may be cascading down to the link elements, and update those as needed.
  • Verify the Noto Sans font is loaded in the theme (via <link> in theme.liquid or via Shopify's font picker settings) so the corrected rule actually renders the intended typeface.
  • Re-run the test at 375 px viewport after the fix to confirm the font-family assertion passes.
 FAIL
#02 Verify xpath=//div[@id='NavDrawer']//a[contains(@class,'mobile-nav__link') and normalize-space()='Explore'] style font-weight = "700" Same Bold/700 expectation as desktop (H5 - Navi Bar) - currently 300/Light
⚠ ErrorStyle "font-weight" expected "700" but got "300"
🔍 Element Inspector · <a> verify_style click to zoom
🔍 Root Cause
[A] WEBSITE BUG — The active navigation link mobile-nav__link--top-level for the "Explore" item (the current page, indicated by data-active="true") is rendering with font-weight: 300 instead of the expected font-weight: 700. According to the Figma spec, the active/current top-level mobile nav link should be visually distinguished with bold (700) font weight. The theme CSS is either missing a rule for [data-active="true"] on .mobile-nav__link, or an existing rule is being overridden by a lower-specificity or conflicting declaration that sets font-weight: 300.
❌ Problematic Code
/* Current theme CSS — no bold rule for active state, or overridden by something like: */
.mobile-nav__link {
  font-weight: 300; /* applies to all states including active */
}
/* Missing or insufficient rule: */
/* .mobile-nav__link[data-active="true"] { font-weight: 700; } */
✅ Fixed Code
/* Add to theme CSS (e.g., theme.css or mobile-nav section styles) */
.mobile-nav__link[data-active="true"],
.mobile-nav__link--top-level[data-active="true"] {
  font-weight: 700;
}
📋 What To Do
  • Locate the mobile nav stylesheet in the Shopify theme (likely theme.css, mobile-nav.css, or an inline <style> block in nav-drawer.liquid or mobile-nav.liquid).
  • Add the CSS rule above to ensure data-active="true" links render at font-weight: 700 on the active page.
  • Verify no other rule (e.g., a wildcard or .mobile-nav__link base rule with higher specificity) overrides this; use !important as a last resort if specificity conflicts persist.
  • Re-run the test at 375 px viewport after deploying the fix to confirm font-weight resolves to 700.
